en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll get ready for a job interview in English: describing your experience with proof, telling a STAR story, and talking about your strengths, weaknesses and goals. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: Your experience, with proof
steps.text: Almost every interview starts with 'Tell me about yourself.' Let's build a strong answer.
steps.body: Use three parts: **now** (*I've been working as a … for / since …*), **before** (*Before that, I worked at …*), and **why this job**. Then give **proof**, not just *hard-working*: **I was responsible for …**, **I managed to …** (= berhasil), **I led a team of …**, and **numbers**: *increased sales by 20%*. Careful: *manage* + noun = memimpin (*I managed a team*), but *managed to* + verb = berhasil.

pairs.en: I've been working as a … for / since …
pairs.id: Saya sudah bekerja sebagai … selama / sejak …

pairs.en: I led a team of five.
pairs.id: Saya memimpin tim berisi lima orang.

steps.title: Concrete, not vague
steps.text: Read these aloud. Each one gives a fact the interviewer can believe.
steps.body: Traps: *sejak* isn't always *since*. A **length** of time takes **for** (*for three years*, not *'since three years'*); a **starting point** takes **since** (*since 2021*). *berhasil* is **managed to**, not *'succeeded to'*. *per cent* is British, *percent* American.

examples.en: I've been working as an accountant at a bank in Surabaya for three years.
examples.id: Saya sudah bekerja sebagai akuntan di sebuah bank di Surabaya selama tiga tahun.

examples.en: Before that, I worked at an online shop in Bandung for two years.
examples.id: Sebelumnya, saya bekerja di sebuah toko online di Bandung selama dua tahun.

examples.en: I was responsible for the company's TikTok and Instagram accounts.
examples.id: Saya bertanggung jawab atas akun TikTok dan Instagram perusahaan.

examples.en: I managed to grow our followers from 5,000 to 40,000 in one year.
examples.id: Saya berhasil menambah pengikut kami dari 5.000 menjadi 40.000 dalam satu tahun.

examples.en: I led a team of four, and we reduced printing costs by 30%.
examples.id: Saya memimpin tim berisi empat orang, dan kami menekan biaya cetak sebesar 30%.

steps.title: For or since?
steps.text: Let's check the time words.

question.prompt: The interviewer asks: 'How long have you been working at your current company?' You joined it in 2022, and you still work there. Which answer is correct?
options: I've been working there since three years.
I'm working there since 2022.
I've been working there since 2022.
question.explanation: You still work there, so use the present perfect continuous (**I've been working**), and **since** + a starting point (2022). *since three years* mixes since with a length of time (that needs *for*), and *I'm working there since* uses the present continuous: it can't take since or for.

steps.title: The STAR method
steps.text: Next: questions like 'Tell me about a time when you …'. They have a special name and a special answer.
steps.body: A **behavioural question** (pertanyaan perilaku) asks what you **did** in a real situation. Answer with **STAR**: **S**ituation = the background, short; **T**ask = what you had to do; **A**ction = what **you** did, step by step (the longest part); **R**esult = what happened in the end, with numbers, and what you learnt. It's a story, so use the **past simple** (*I called, I moved*). Say **I**, not *we*, for your own actions: the interviewer is hiring you, not your team.

pairs.en: Tell me about a time when you …

pairs.id: tugasnya: apa yang harus kamu lakukan

steps.title: A full STAR answer
steps.text: Here's a model answer to 'Tell me about a time you solved a problem at work.' Read it aloud and find S, T, A and R.
steps.body: The parts come in order: S (the clinic, the long wait), T (what the manager asked), A (three things *I* did) and R (numbers + a lesson). Notice the past forms: *was working, asked, looked, moved, fell*. *learnt* is British; *learned* works everywhere.

examples.en: Tell me about a time you solved a problem at work.
examples.id: (Pertanyaan) Ceritakan saat kamu menyelesaikan masalah di tempat kerja.

examples.en: Last year, I was working as an admin supervisor at a clinic in Surabaya. Patients were waiting more than an hour.
examples.id: (S) Tahun lalu, saya bekerja sebagai supervisor admin di sebuah klinik di Surabaya. Pasien menunggu lebih dari satu jam.

examples.en: My manager asked me to cut the waiting time before the end of the month.
examples.id: (T) Manajer saya meminta saya memangkas waktu tunggu sebelum akhir bulan.

examples.en: First, I looked at the data. Most patients came between eight and ten.
examples.id: (A) Pertama, saya melihat datanya. Kebanyakan pasien datang antara jam delapan dan sepuluh.

examples.en: So I moved two staff to the morning shift and set up online booking through WhatsApp.
examples.id: (A) Jadi saya memindahkan dua staf ke shift pagi dan membuat pendaftaran online lewat WhatsApp.

examples.en: As a result, the waiting time fell from 70 to 25 minutes. I learnt that the data often shows the real problem.
examples.id: (R) Hasilnya, waktu tunggu turun dari 70 menjadi 25 menit. Saya belajar bahwa data sering menunjukkan masalah yang sebenarnya.

steps.title: Finish the story
steps.text: Rina's STAR answer is missing its last part. Help her.

question.prompt: Rina's answer. S: Our online shop was getting a lot of complaints about late deliveries. T: I had to fix it before the 12.12 sale. A: I compared three couriers, chose a faster one and checked every order myself. Which sentence is the best Result?
options: We always try our best to make our customers happy.
As a result, late deliveries fell from 30% of orders to 5%, and we got our best reviews ever during the sale.
In the end, I finish the problem and everything is good.
question.explanation: A good Result says what happened in the end, in the **past simple**, with **numbers** (*fell from 30% … to 5%*). The first option is general and in the present: it's not part of the story. The third has no past forms (*finish, is*) and no facts.

steps.title: Strengths and weaknesses
steps.text: Two classic questions: 'What's your main strength?' and 'What's your biggest weakness?'
steps.body: **Strength:** name **one**, then prove it: **My main strength is** + noun (*teamwork, problem-solving*) … **For example, …** + a true story with a number. **Weakness:** choose something real but not a disaster for the job, and say how you're improving: **I sometimes find it hard to …, so I'm working on it by …**. Watch two habits: **too modest** (the *'saya masih belajar'* style: *Sorry, I'm still learning*) sounds unsure; **too proud** (*I'm the best, I can do everything*) is hard to believe. The middle way: facts.

pairs.en: I sometimes find it hard to …
so I'm working on it by …
I've been taking an online course in …

steps.title: Your main strength
steps.text: Which answer would convince you if you were the interviewer?

question.prompt: Sari is interviewing for a job at a supermarket chain in Jakarta. The manager asks: 'What's your main strength?' Which answer is best?
options: My main strength is problem-solving. For example, when our cashier system went down last month, I set up a manual process in ten minutes, so we didn't lose any sales.
My main strength is that I'm very hard-working, smart, creative, friendly and honest.
Sorry, I don't think I have a real strength yet. I'm still learning.
question.explanation: It names **one** strength and proves it with **For example** + a real story with a result. A long list of adjectives proves nothing, and the third answer is far too modest: in an English interview it sounds like you have no skills.

steps.title: Listen and reply
steps.text: Press play and listen to the interviewer's question.

question.prompt: Listen to the interviewer's question. Which reply is best?
question.listen: And what would you say is your biggest weakness?
options: I don't have any weaknesses. I'm good at everything.
Sorry, I'm still learning, so I have a lot of weaknesses.
I sometimes get nervous when I present to large groups, so I've been giving short presentations at our weekly team meeting to get more practice.
question.explanation: The interviewer asks about your **biggest weakness**. The best reply is honest, real and shows what you're doing about it (*I've been giving short presentations …*). *I don't have any weaknesses* is overclaiming, and *I have a lot of weaknesses* is too modest and doesn't name one.

steps.title: Goals and your own questions
steps.text: Last part: the future, and the end of the interview.
steps.body: *Where do you see yourself in five years?* → **In five years, I'd like to …** / **I'm hoping to …** / **My long-term goal is to …** (*I'd like* sounds more polite than *I want*). At the end you'll hear *Do you have any questions for us?* Always ask one: *No questions* can sound uninterested. **Personal details:** Indonesian CVs often list religion and marital status, but in many countries interviewers avoid these topics, so you don't need to mention them unprompted.

pairs.en: In five years, I'd like to …
What are the biggest challenges for the team right now?
pairs.id: Apa tantangan terbesar tim saat ini?

pairs.en: What training do new staff get?
pairs.id: Pelatihan apa yang didapat staf baru?

pairs.en: What are the next steps in the process?
pairs.id: Apa tahap berikutnya dalam proses ini?

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's your interview kit on one page. Read it again the night before.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · job interviews
artifact.intro: Say how long with for/since, prove your experience with numbers, tell STAR stories in the past simple with I, and talk about strengths, weaknesses and goals with facts.
rows: I've been working as a … for three years / since 2022.
Before that, I worked at … for two years.
I was responsible for … / I led a team of …
I managed to cut costs by 15%.
Last year, I was working as …
My manager asked me to … / I had to …
First, I … Then I … I also …
As a result, … fell / rose by … I learnt that …
My main strength is … For example, …
I sometimes find it hard to …, so I'm working on it by …
In five years, I'd like to … / I'm hoping to …
dalam lima tahun, saya ingin … / berharap …
What does a typical day look like in this role?
seperti apa hari kerja biasa di posisi ini?
What are the next steps in the process?
tips: Not 'since three years' but for three years; not 'succeeded to' but managed to; not 'many experiences' but five years of experience.
In a STAR story, use past forms and say I for your own actions, not we.
Not too modest, not too proud: let facts and numbers speak. No need to mention religion or marital status unprompted.

examples.en: I've been working in customer service for five years.
examples.id: Saya sudah bekerja di layanan pelanggan selama lima tahun.

examples.en: I managed to reduce complaints by half in three months.
examples.id: Saya berhasil mengurangi keluhan sampai separuhnya dalam tiga bulan.

examples.en: My main strength is attention to detail. For example, I found a 40-million-rupiah mistake in our tax report.
examples.id: Kekuatan utama saya adalah ketelitian. Contohnya, saya menemukan kesalahan 40 juta rupiah di laporan pajak kami.

examples.en: In five years, I'm hoping to lead a small team here.
examples.id: Dalam lima tahun, saya berharap bisa memimpin tim kecil di sini.

steps.text: Want more practice? Here's a video about STAR answers and an article on preparing for an interview in English.

id.greeting: Halo! Hari ini kamu bersiap untuk wawancara kerja dalam bahasa Inggris: menjelaskan pengalamanmu dengan bukti, menceritakan kisah STAR, dan membicarakan kekuatan, kelemahan serta tujuanmu. Ayo kita mulai langkah demi langkah.

steps.title: Pengalamanmu, dengan bukti
steps.text: Hampir setiap wawancara dimulai dengan 'Tell me about yourself' (ceritakan tentang dirimu). Ayo susun jawaban yang kuat.
steps.body: Pakai tiga bagian: **sekarang** (*I've been working as a … for / since …*), **sebelumnya** (*Before that, I worked at …*), dan **kenapa pekerjaan ini**. Lalu beri **bukti**, bukan cuma *hard-working*: **I was responsible for …** (bertanggung jawab atas), **I managed to …** (= berhasil), **I led a team of …** (memimpin tim), dan **angka**: *increased sales by 20%*. Hati-hati: *manage* + kata benda = memimpin (*I managed a team*), tapi *managed to* + kata kerja = berhasil.

pairs.en: I've been working as a … for / since …
pairs.id: Saya sudah bekerja sebagai … selama / sejak …

pairs.en: I led a team of five.
pairs.id: Saya memimpin tim berisi lima orang.

steps.title: Konkret, bukan samar
steps.text: Baca kalimat-kalimat ini dengan suara keras. Masing-masing memberi fakta yang bisa dipercaya pewawancara.
steps.body: Jebakan: *sejak* tidak selalu *since*. **Lamanya** waktu pakai **for** (*for three years*, bukan *'since three years'*); **titik mulai** pakai **since** (*since 2021*). *berhasil* adalah **managed to**, bukan *'succeeded to'*. *per cent* itu British, *percent* Amerika.

examples.en: I've been working as an accountant at a bank in Surabaya for three years.
examples.id: Saya sudah bekerja sebagai akuntan di sebuah bank di Surabaya selama tiga tahun.

examples.en: Before that, I worked at an online shop in Bandung for two years.
examples.id: Sebelumnya, saya bekerja di sebuah toko online di Bandung selama dua tahun.

examples.en: I was responsible for the company's TikTok and Instagram accounts.
examples.id: Saya bertanggung jawab atas akun TikTok dan Instagram perusahaan.

examples.en: I managed to grow our followers from 5,000 to 40,000 in one year.
examples.id: Saya berhasil menambah pengikut kami dari 5.000 menjadi 40.000 dalam satu tahun.

examples.en: I led a team of four, and we reduced printing costs by 30%.
examples.id: Saya memimpin tim berisi empat orang, dan kami menekan biaya cetak sebesar 30%.

steps.title: For atau since?
steps.text: Ayo cek kata-kata waktunya.

question.prompt: Pewawancara bertanya: 'How long have you been working at your current company?' Kamu masuk ke perusahaan itu tahun 2022, dan masih bekerja di sana. Jawaban mana yang benar?
options: I've been working there since three years.
I'm working there since 2022.
I've been working there since 2022.
question.explanation: Kamu masih bekerja di sana, jadi pakai present perfect continuous (**I've been working**), dan **since** + titik mulai (2022). *since three years* mencampur since dengan lamanya waktu (itu butuh *for*), dan *I'm working there since* memakai present continuous, yang tidak bisa dipakai dengan since atau for.

steps.title: Metode STAR
steps.text: Berikutnya: pertanyaan seperti 'Tell me about a time when you …'. Pertanyaan ini punya nama khusus dan cara menjawab yang khusus.
steps.body: **Behavioural question** (pertanyaan perilaku) menanyakan apa yang **kamu lakukan** dalam situasi nyata. Jawab dengan **STAR**: **S**ituation = latar belakangnya, singkat; **T**ask = apa yang harus kamu lakukan; **A**ction = apa yang **kamu** lakukan, langkah demi langkah (bagian terpanjang); **R**esult = apa yang terjadi pada akhirnya, dengan angka, dan apa yang kamu pelajari. Ini cerita, jadi pakai **past simple** (*I called, I moved*). Pakai **I**, bukan *we*, untuk tindakanmu sendiri: yang direkrut kamu, bukan timmu.

pairs.en: Tell me about a time when you …

pairs.id: tugasnya: apa yang harus kamu lakukan

steps.title: Satu jawaban STAR lengkap
steps.text: Ini contoh jawaban untuk 'Tell me about a time you solved a problem at work.' Baca dengan suara keras dan temukan S, T, A dan R.
steps.body: Bagian-bagiannya berurutan: S (kliniknya, antrean panjang), T (apa yang diminta manajer), A (tiga hal yang *saya* lakukan) dan R (angka + pelajaran). Perhatikan bentuk lampaunya: *was working, asked, looked, moved, fell*. *learnt* itu British; *learned* bisa dipakai di mana saja.

examples.en: Tell me about a time you solved a problem at work.
examples.id: (Pertanyaan) Ceritakan saat kamu menyelesaikan masalah di tempat kerja.

examples.en: Last year, I was working as an admin supervisor at a clinic in Surabaya. Patients were waiting more than an hour.
examples.id: (S) Tahun lalu, saya bekerja sebagai supervisor admin di sebuah klinik di Surabaya. Pasien menunggu lebih dari satu jam.

examples.en: My manager asked me to cut the waiting time before the end of the month.
examples.id: (T) Manajer saya meminta saya memangkas waktu tunggu sebelum akhir bulan.

examples.en: First, I looked at the data. Most patients came between eight and ten.
examples.id: (A) Pertama, saya melihat datanya. Kebanyakan pasien datang antara jam delapan dan sepuluh.

examples.en: So I moved two staff to the morning shift and set up online booking through WhatsApp.
examples.id: (A) Jadi saya memindahkan dua staf ke shift pagi dan membuat pendaftaran online lewat WhatsApp.

examples.en: As a result, the waiting time fell from 70 to 25 minutes. I learnt that the data often shows the real problem.
examples.id: (R) Hasilnya, waktu tunggu turun dari 70 menjadi 25 menit. Saya belajar bahwa data sering menunjukkan masalah yang sebenarnya.

steps.title: Selesaikan ceritanya
steps.text: Jawaban STAR Rina belum ada bagian terakhirnya. Bantu dia.

question.prompt: Jawaban Rina. S: Our online shop was getting a lot of complaints about late deliveries. T: I had to fix it before the 12.12 sale. A: I compared three couriers, chose a faster one and checked every order myself. Kalimat mana yang paling baik untuk Result?
options: We always try our best to make our customers happy.
As a result, late deliveries fell from 30% of orders to 5%, and we got our best reviews ever during the sale.
In the end, I finish the problem and everything is good.
question.explanation: Result yang baik menyebut apa yang terjadi pada akhirnya, dengan **past simple** dan **angka** (*fell from 30% … to 5%*). Pilihan pertama umum dan memakai present: bukan bagian dari ceritanya. Pilihan ketiga tidak punya bentuk lampau (*finish, is*) dan tidak ada faktanya.

steps.title: Kekuatan dan kelemahan
steps.text: Dua pertanyaan klasik: 'What's your main strength?' dan 'What's your biggest weakness?'
steps.body: **Kekuatan:** sebutkan **satu**, lalu buktikan: **My main strength is** + kata benda (*teamwork, problem-solving*) … **For example, …** + cerita nyata dengan angka. **Kelemahan:** pilih sesuatu yang nyata tapi tidak fatal untuk pekerjaannya, dan katakan cara kamu memperbaikinya: **I sometimes find it hard to …, so I'm working on it by …**. Waspadai dua kebiasaan: **terlalu merendah** (gaya *'saya masih belajar'*: *Sorry, I'm still learning*) terdengar tidak yakin; **terlalu membanggakan diri** (*I'm the best, I can do everything*) sulit dipercaya. Jalan tengahnya: fakta.

pairs.en: I sometimes find it hard to …
so I'm working on it by …
I've been taking an online course in …

steps.title: Kekuatan utamamu
steps.text: Jawaban mana yang akan meyakinkanmu kalau kamu pewawancaranya?

question.prompt: Sari sedang wawancara untuk pekerjaan di sebuah jaringan supermarket di Jakarta. Manajernya bertanya: 'What's your main strength?' Jawaban mana yang paling baik?
options: My main strength is problem-solving. For example, when our cashier system went down last month, I set up a manual process in ten minutes, so we didn't lose any sales.
My main strength is that I'm very hard-working, smart, creative, friendly and honest.
Sorry, I don't think I have a real strength yet. I'm still learning.
question.explanation: Jawaban ini menyebut **satu** kekuatan dan membuktikannya dengan **For example** + cerita nyata yang ada hasilnya. Daftar panjang kata sifat tidak membuktikan apa pun, dan jawaban ketiga jauh terlalu merendah: di wawancara berbahasa Inggris, itu terdengar seperti kamu tidak punya kemampuan.

steps.title: Dengarkan dan jawab
steps.text: Tekan play dan dengarkan pertanyaan pewawancara.

question.prompt: Dengarkan pertanyaan pewawancara. Jawaban mana yang paling baik?
question.listen: And what would you say is your biggest weakness?
options: I don't have any weaknesses. I'm good at everything.
Sorry, I'm still learning, so I have a lot of weaknesses.
I sometimes get nervous when I present to large groups, so I've been giving short presentations at our weekly team meeting to get more practice.
question.explanation: Pewawancara bertanya tentang **kelemahan terbesarmu** (biggest weakness). Jawaban terbaik itu jujur, nyata, dan menunjukkan apa yang sedang kamu lakukan untuk memperbaikinya (*I've been giving short presentations …*). *I don't have any weaknesses* terlalu membanggakan diri, dan *I have a lot of weaknesses* terlalu merendah dan tidak menyebut satu pun.

steps.title: Tujuan dan pertanyaanmu sendiri
steps.text: Bagian terakhir: masa depan, dan akhir wawancara.
steps.body: *Where do you see yourself in five years?* → **In five years, I'd like to …** / **I'm hoping to …** / **My long-term goal is to …** (*I'd like* terdengar lebih sopan daripada *I want*). Di akhir kamu akan mendengar *Do you have any questions for us?* Selalu ajukan satu pertanyaan: *tidak ada pertanyaan* bisa terdengar tidak tertarik. **Data pribadi:** CV di Indonesia sering mencantumkan agama dan status pernikahan, tapi di banyak negara pewawancara menghindari topik ini, jadi kamu tidak perlu menyebutnya kalau tidak ditanya.

pairs.en: In five years, I'd like to …
What are the biggest challenges for the team right now?
pairs.id: Apa tantangan terbesar tim saat ini?

pairs.en: What training do new staff get?
pairs.id: Pelatihan apa yang didapat staf baru?

pairs.en: What are the next steps in the process?
pairs.id: Apa tahap berikutnya dalam proses ini?

steps.text: Ini perlengkapan wawancaramu dalam satu halaman. Baca lagi malam sebelum wawancara.
